name: Inventurus Knowledge Solutions Ltd
title: Inventurus Knowledge Solutions Ltd - 544309 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Revenue up 18.5% YoY to INR857 crore with PAT up 48% to INR721 crore for FY26, but this is a services/RCM story with no capacity or pricing supply signal; headcount rose 5.3% YoY and the TruBridge debt-funded deal takes leverage to about 3x.

guidance.value: INR3,000 crore by FY30 from ~INR1,000 crore LTM Dec 2025
guidance.quote: INR1,000 crore odd mark LTM December 2025 to INR3,000 in FY30

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18.5% YoY to INR857 crore and EBITDA margin hit about 35%, with PAT of INR206 crore, alongside a pending TruBridge acquisition.
summary.overview: Management reported its sixth consecutive quarter of growth, with Q4 FY26 revenue of about INR857 crore (up 18.5% YoY, 5.2% QoQ), EBITDA of about INR300 crore (35% margin), and PAT of INR206 crore (up 39% YoY). FY26 revenue was INR3,193 crore (up 20%), EBITDA INR1,091 crore (up 34%) and PAT INR721 crore (up 48%). Management said the company is pivoting its go-to-market toward land-and-expand with system-owned provider groups, and is pursuing AI-native products and the pending TruBridge acquisition. Headcount rose to 13,331 from 12,661 but fell 5.2% QoQ. Management declined to give quantitative guidance beyond an FY27 effective tax rate of about 22%.

financial_highlights.change: FY27 guided at about 22% for IKS standalone
down from a peak of about INR850 crore
slight decline due to revaluation of an equity holding and rupee depreciation effect

financial_highlights.metric: Net forex and hedge impact in Q4
financial_highlights.value: INR23 crore net benefit (INR35 crore forex gain less INR12 crore hedge loss)

segments.name: RCM (revenue cycle management)
segments.commentary: Management described RCM as the primary buying entry point for system-owned provider groups, with ambulatory RCM recognised by KLAS and Black Book. Management also cited a top health system win for RCM and value-based care.

segments.name: AI products (Select, MyCare Hub, Certilytics, ThinkDTM)
segments.commentary: Select is a multi-variant AI scribing product, with a clinician in the loop for complex encounters and fully AI for simpler ones; management cited high accuracy in two specialties. MyCare Hub is a multi-agent patient engagement product that ThinkDTM brought in through an acqui-hire, and it and the cycle engine are now available on Epic Connection Hub.

segments.name: Holyoke Medical Center (client win)
segments.commentary: Management announced a win for the entire IKS platform at Holyoke Medical Center. It did not give a financial size.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative guidance on revenue, margin or growth; management said it does not guide on any single parameter.
Effective tax rate for FY27 is expected at about 22% for the IKS standalone business; consolidated ETR will be shared after the TruBridge deal closes.
Q1 CY26 (Q1 FY27) is seasonally the weakest quarter for US providers, with low patient footfall; other expenses will rise in Q1 from one-time TruBridge deal costs.
Aspirational target: grow from about INR1,000 crore (LTM Dec 2025) to INR3,000 crore by FY30, with net zero debt targeted in that period.
Management expects the TruBridge deal to be leveraged at about 3x at close, with deleveraging through internal accruals; regulatory approvals are in progress.
capex_capacity: Headcount at 31 March 2026 was 13,331 (1,981 clinically trained), up from 12,661 a year earlier and down 5.2% QoQ from about 14,000 in December 2025 (as stated in the call).
About 550 employees are focused on AI engineering and data science; sales and marketing headcount is 66 FTEs and growing.
The company is migrating its EHR from legacy platforms to PostgreSQL; management expects this to take about two years, with the RCM business largely independent of the migration.
TruBridge acquisition (EHR in about 700 to 800 hospitals; about 2,200 hospitals in the segment, per management) is awaiting regulatory approval after signing.
demand_pricing: Client count is about 600 organisations, down from about 700 at IPO and about 900 at the AQuity acquisition, reflecting tail-client pruning; about 450 are enterprise clients.
About 90% of revenue is repeat business; top 10 and top 5 client vintage averages 5 to 6 years.
Pricing is partly outcome-based, which management said gives a margin advantage when AI reduces effort; management said AI-led deflation pressure has not been seen yet.
Competition is split into EHR vendors, point-solution vendors and platform players; management said entry barriers are lowest for point-solution players and that consolidation is expected.
Management said the company has not received any pricing pushback so far and that its AI pricing is per feature, not per seat.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company approaching a possible CommonSpirit Health opportunity and Epic marketplace listings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on specific opportunities. It said CommonSpirit is on its radar as ministries are unbundled from the Tenet arrangement, and that it has a history working with several CommonSpirit ministries.

qa_highlights.question: How will the tech stack for the ambulatory and acute platforms converge after integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is zero actual overlap in customers, but it will modernise the EHR to PostgreSQL and integrate its AI corpus, a roughly two-year journey for the core EHR.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from cheaper AI for the business model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cheaper AI generation is a tailwind, since IKS builds its own AI and is paid for outcomes rather than effort.

qa_highlights.question: When will growth stop being lumpy, and can the company catch up on growth after six quarters of strong growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance and said the journey is not linear. It pointed to the 3x revenue target to FY30 and a 12% share of its TAM.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company seeing AI-driven productivity pressure on pricing, as IT and BPO peers reported?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its pricing is outcome-based and not purely effort-based, so AI productivity gains flow to margins. It said some workflows are easily automated and get priced accordingly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost run-rate and ETR outlook for FY27, and is the ETR for IKS or consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: The FY27 ETR of about 22% applies to IKS standalone; consolidated figures will come after the TruBridge deal closes. Management does not guide on individual cost parameters and uses incentives to align employees.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any overlap between TruBridge's EHR and IKS's offerings, and what is the plan for EHR share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TruBridge's EHR serves about 700 hospitals, roughly 35% of a segment of about 2,200 hospitals, dominated by MEDITECH and MEDHOST. The priority is modernising the EHR and deploying IKS services, not gaining EHR share, and management said it would not bank on share gains.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider acquisitions, and how will the TruBridge deal be financed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TruBridge would be funded with debt at about 3x leverage at close, with deleveraging from accruals. It expects tuck-in deals to continue, but not transformative ones soon, and it wants to avoid equity dilution.

risks_watch: TruBridge acquisition: regulatory approvals pending, about 3x leverage at close, and one-time deal costs in Q1 FY27.
Q1 FY27 seasonality: US patient footfall is weakest in Q1 CY, and management flagged higher other expenses.
EHR modernisation to PostgreSQL is a roughly two-year process with migration risk. Management said the RCM business is independent, but the migration could impede EHR-linked product rollout.
Competitive intensity from private equity-backed RCM players (for example Carlyle deals) and consolidation in the US RCM market.
Client count is falling (about 600 from about 700 at IPO) through tail-client pruning, and the company is pivoting to system-owned provider groups with an unproven land-and-expand motion.
Q4 PAT margin quality: finance costs fell after a Q3 one-off write-off, and the ROE decline is partly due to revaluation and rupee depreciation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margin and AI strategy, with explicit reluctance to give guidance or predict quarterly rates. Evasive on TruBridge integration details and specific client opportunities, citing the pending deal and confidentiality.

growth.why: No quantitative FY27 revenue guidance; management declined to guide on growth, only giving a ~22% FY27 tax rate. Q4 revenue grew 18.5% YoY and the only forward marker is an aspirational INR3,000 crore by FY30 with no capacity, orders or timing behind it, so backing is vague.
